text:
Marta: Heads-up — pushed a new mock for the API Keys list view (table + action menu). Wanted a quick UX + a11y pass before we lock copy. Figma link: https://figma.com/...

Devon: Taking a look now. First pass: love the condensed rows but a couple of concerns about the action menu density.

Devon: Question — should Rotate and Revoke be primary actions in the row, or tucked into kebab?

Marta: We initially put Rotate as an inline button because it's common, revoke in kebab. But worried about accidental clicks and discoverability.

Izzy: My vote: keep Rotate inline but make it a secondary (ghost) button with a confirmation step. Revoke stays in kebab to reduce accidental usage.

Linus: Agree with Izzy. Also can we add a small tooltip on hover for Rotate: "Creates a new key and retires the old one — update integrations" ? :eyes:

Marta: Good call. Tooltip text sounds right. Also we should clarify rotate semantics in the modal: whether old key remains valid for X mins.

Devon: For the rotate modal copy: current draft says:

```
Rotate API key?
This will create a new key and stop traffic on the old one immediately.
```

Devon: Suggest change to:

```
Rotate API key?
A new key will be created immediately. The old key will be revoked after 5 minutes to give you a short migration window.
```

Izzy: +1. That migration window is critical to avoid breaking customers. Also link to troubleshooting doc (internal).

Marta: Revoke modal currently demands typing the key name to confirm. Is that overkill? We wanted a high-friction pattern for revoke.

Linus: Typing the key name is good for org-owned or global keys. For user-scoped keys maybe require just a checkbox because it hinders frequent ops. Could be configurable based on permission level.

Marta: Good point. How do we signal permission levels in the UI? e.g., some users can only create keys with limited scopes.

Devon: Proposal: show a tiny role badge next to Create button: "You can create: read-only, embeddings-only". If you lack create perms, hide the button and show a subtle empty state CTA with link to request access.

Izzy: Please ensure request flow is keyboard accessible. Empty state CTA must be focusable and announced by screen readers.

a11y-bot: Automated suggestion — focus order on the table needs to be: checkbox -> key name -> scopes -> created date -> actions. Current mock places created date before scopes which is confusing when tabbing. Also ensure actions menu is reachable by Enter/Space and that menu items have role="menuitem" and aria-labels: "Rotate key <key-name>", "Revoke key <key-name>".

Marta: Thanks @a11y-bot. We had a weird tab jump because of the inline tooltip being focusable. We'll make tooltips non-focusable and only the trigger is focusable.

Devon: Another small thing: keyboard users expect a dedicated keyboard shortcut to open actions on the focused row, like pressing "." to open kebab. Maybe too fancy?

Izzy: Let's skip custom shortcuts for now. Stick to native keyboard patterns and ensure Enter on the actions button opens the menu.

Linus: On empty states — current copy: "No API keys yet". Suggest more actionable copy: "No API keys yet — create a key to start making requests" + primary CTA "Create API key" and secondary link "Learn about key best practices".

Marta: Love that. Also add a small security callout for org admins: "Recommended: restrict keys by scope and rotate periodically." Could be collapsed by default.

Devon: Minor visual nit — when a key is newly created, we show the secret in a toast. Ensure the toast has role="alert" and is keyboard dismissible; also provide a copy button with aria-label "Copy secret for <key-name>".

a11y-bot: Suggestion — for toasts that contain secrets, avoid auto-dismiss or allow a longer timeout and ensure the secret is hidden behind a reveal button for screen readers. Also mark the secret value with aria-live="polite" only after user reveals it.

Marta: That makes sense. We'll change to a modal reveal that requires a copy click (less likely to be missed).

Devon: One more decide: do we surface scopes inline as pills or a collapsed count (e.g., "3 scopes") with popup on hover? Large scope lists make rows tall.

Izzy: Collapsed count + popover sounds good. Popover must be accessible (focus trap, escape closes). Pills in expanded view fine.

Linus: I'll update the Figma: make Rotate secondary inline, Revoke in kebab, adjust tab order per @a11y-bot, change revoke confirmation dynamic by permission, and switch secret reveal to modal.

Marta: Awesome — thanks everyone. If nobody objects I'll push the copy tweaks and accessibility notes into the component ticket after lunch. :thumbsup:

Devon: No objections. Can you also add the troubleshooting link and the migration window note in the rotate modal copy?

Marta: Yup — will do.

Linus: ETA for updated mock: EOD.

Izzy: I'll follow up with test cases for keyboard/voiceover tomorrow.

Marta: Great — closing this thread after updates.
